title: DECISION: 10 of 33 commits carry Co-Authored-By: Claude trailers on the public repo
description: Commits 0133c25, 65ade01, fbb7986, b33ed74, 9546e9b, 5060ac8, ad18337, 45c778f, 763174f, 3cedd4f. GitHub renders a Claude avatar next to each on the commits tab. The affected commits are the inline-SVG snake migration, the svgOrigin pupil-tracking and tongue-flick fixes, and the pricing/CTA redesign — the strongest authorship evidence in the repo. Blocked on a decision, not on work: stripping the trailers means git filter-branch/filter-repo across 33 commits plus a force push to master, which rewrites public history. NOT actioned in this session for that reason. Detail and exact line references in AUDIT-2026-08-07.md (untracked, repo root).
design: Option A: git filter-repo --message-callback stripping the trailer, then force push. Option B: leave it. Option C: squash history into a fresh initial commit. Mike's call.
acceptance_criteria: Decision recorded; if A or C, history rewritten and force-pushed, and the Vercel deployment still resolves.

title: README is the repo's first screen and it misdescribes the project
description: Public repo, linked as the portfolio piece. README.md:34 points at .impeccable.md which does not exist anywhere in the repo. Line 18 claims 'Tailwind v4 (utilities)' but there is not a single Tailwind utility class in src/ — the CSS file uses @theme token bridging and the components use inline styles, which is the more interesting story anyway. Lines 36-38 claim MIT but there is no LICENSE file and package.json has no license key. No link to the live site and no screenshot, in a repo whose whole subject is visual. Detail and exact line references in AUDIT-2026-08-07.md (untracked, repo root).
acceptance_criteria: Every claim in README verifiable; live URL linked above the fold; one screenshot embedded; LICENSE present or the claim dropped.
close_reason: fixed in the parallel lane run; build+lint green, verified in-browser at 390/768/820/1280/1440

title: WCAG AA: --muted body copy is 4.49:1 and white-on-accent CTA text is 3.68:1
description: Ratios recomputed by the audit. --muted #5d6f9e on --bg #eef4ff = 4.49:1, under 4.5 by a hair, and it colors the hero subhead, every section paragraph, every mono eyebrow and the pricing commentary. White on --accent #3b82f6 = 3.68:1 across all three 'add to messenger' CTAs — none qualify as WCAG large text (largest is 18px/700, threshold is 18.66px bold). The receipt total is 3.62:1. The unused whatsscribe --muted is worse at 4.25:1. Detail and exact line references in AUDIT-2026-08-07.md (untracked, repo root).
design: Suggested: --muted #586a99 (4.83:1 on bg, visually indistinguishable). For the CTA, a separate darker token used only for solid accent fills — #2563eb is 5.17:1 against white — keeping --accent itself for text, borders and the 'sssuddenly' headline. NOTE: changing the accent is a brand decision, needs Mike's sign-off before wiring.
acceptance_criteria: All body copy and CTA labels pass AA; brand blue still reads as the same blue.
notes:
PARTIAL. The --muted half is done: #5d6f9e -> #55679b (messscribe, 5.01:1 on --bg) and #5b7a64 -> #4f6b57 (whatsscribe, 5.24:1). Verified in-browser.

Still open, and deliberately so: white-on---accent CTA text at 3.68:1. --accent-strong (#2563eb messscribe / #14783c whatsscribe, both >5:1 white-on) is now DEFINED in index.css but wired to nothing, so switching the CTA fill is a one-line change whenever the owner decides.

Narrower than it looks: .cta-btn:hover and :focus-visible already set background: var(--ink), so only the REST state fails. The receipt total in pricing-section.tsx:116 (accent on #fffdf7, 3.62:1) is the same decision.

title: body never paints the page ground — white flash before hydration and white overscroll gutters
description: index.css:73 sets body{background:var(--bg)} but --bg is only defined on .theme-messscribe, a class applied to a div inside #root. The declaration is invalid at computed-value time, so the canvas falls back to UA white: the viewport stays white until the JS chunk mounts React then snaps to #eef4ff, and rubber-band overscroll shows white above the hero and below the navy footer. Detail and exact line references in AUDIT-2026-08-07.md (untracked, repo root).
design: Promote the messscribe token set (--bg,--fg,--accent,--accent-2,--ink,--muted,--card) to :root as the default, keeping .theme-messscribe/.theme-whatsscribe as overrides — the existing body rule then resolves at first paint and the theme-swap architecture is untouched.
acceptance_criteria: No white flash on hard reload; overscroll gutters match the page ground top and bottom.
close_reason: fixed in the parallel lane run; build+lint green, verified in-browser at 390/768/820/1280/1440

title: hero: yolk disc escapes its column at 768-900px and the snake/disc ratio swings 68-123%
description: The yolk disc at hero-section.tsx:155-166 is position:absolute so it contributes no height. At 768px it computes to 500x500 inside a column only as tall as the snake (~338px), bleeding ~81px above and below: it covers the CTA row and the 'no sign-up' line, and punches through the marquee band beneath. iPad portrait (810-820px) sits inside the broken band. Same root cause drives a second symptom — disc is sized min(82%,500px) while the snake is clamp(220px,min(100%,44vw),560px), so the mascot fills 68% of the circle at 768px and overflows it at 123% at 1024px. Only 1440px looks intentional. Detail and exact line references in AUDIT-2026-08-07.md (untracked, repo root).
design: Give the art column a real square box (width:min(82%,500px); aspect-ratio:1) carrying the disc, with snake and sticker positioned inside it. Then size the snake as a fixed percentage of that box (~96%) so the ratio is constant and only the disc scales.
acceptance_criteria: No overlap of the disc with the CTA row or marquee at any width 360-1600px; snake-to-disc ratio visually constant across that range.
close_reason: fixed in the parallel lane run; build+lint green, verified in-browser at 390/768/820/1280/1440

title: README still has no image, on a repo whose whole subject is visual
description:
The README now links the live site, but contains no screenshot. For a portfolio piece about visual craft, a reviewer reading the repo before clicking through sees only prose.

Not done during the README rewrite because the ~31 loose PNGs in the repo root are untracked iteration scratch, and promoting one blind would have committed an arbitrary work-in-progress frame.

Needs: one clean 1440px capture of the live site (hero is the strongest single frame — the yolk disc and mascot are the identity), committed to public/ or docs/, embedded under the live-site link. public/og-image.png is 1200x630 and already brand-correct if a purpose-built graphic is preferred to a screenshot.

title: storyboard mock text renders at 7-9px on phones
description: The how-it-works section's job is showing the three-step flow, and at 390px it degrades into texture. Hardcoded sizes that don't scale: storyboard.tsx:117 ('0:34' at 9px), :128-148 (the chips at 9px), :195-215 ('typing...' at 8px). Two of them are also sub-AA: 'typing...' is white@40% on --ink (3.71:1) and the 'reply' chip is white@50% on white@10% (3.90:1). Detail and exact line references in AUDIT-2026-08-07.md (untracked, repo root).
design: Floor the mockup type at 11px on narrow viewports with a mobile override on the sub-10px labels; raise the dim whites from 0.4/0.5 alpha to 0.6/0.7.
acceptance_criteria: No text under 11px at 390px; dim whites pass AA.
close_reason: fixed in the parallel lane run; build+lint green, verified in-browser at 390/768/820/1280/1440

title: RTL: the Arabic sample renders mangled in the section built to demo multilingual support
description: With no bidi isolation the confidence label at chat-preview.tsx:135-137 reorders to read '95 · العربية% CONFIDENCE' instead of 'العربية · 95% confidence', and the transcript at :139 is left-aligned LTR so the sentence-final period lands on the wrong visual side. Separately index.html sets lang=en and nothing overrides it, so a screen reader pronounces the Portuguese, Spanish, Hindi, Arabic, Chinese and French samples with an English voice. The section's claim is 'works in every language, not just english' and the one RTL language in the picker is the one that breaks. Detail and exact line references in AUDIT-2026-08-07.md (untracked, repo root).
design: dir='auto' on the transcript div, wrap the language name in <bdi>, and add lang (plus dir for Arabic) to TranscriptSample in src/lib/transcripts.ts, spread onto the transcript div and pill labels.
acceptance_criteria: Arabic sample reads correctly right-to-left with the label in the right order.
close_reason: fixed in the parallel lane run; build+lint green, verified in-browser at 390/768/820/1280/1440

title: interaction vocabulary: inert language pills hover like buttons, real flag chips don't
description: The page teaches 'flag pill = clickable' in the live-preview section, then serves 25 pills in the yellow band that aren't. index.css:274-283 gives .lang-pill a 140ms translate plus a 3px hard ink shadow — the page's own press-and-lift language — on non-interactive spans; cursor:default is the only signal otherwise. The last entry compounds it: '+ 24 more' is expand-affordance copy given the inverted ink/accent-2 treatment, which is exactly how chat-preview styles the SELECTED language button. Meanwhile the six real flag buttons at chat-preview.tsx:193-211 have no hover state at all (their transition only fires on the post-click state change), no designed focus ring, no aria-pressed, and a 1px ink border where the system floor is 1.5px. The swapped transcript is never announced. Detail and exact line references in AUDIT-2026-08-07.md (untracked, repo root).
design: Delete the .lang-pill:hover block and move that lift onto the chat-preview flag buttons. Render '+ 24 more' as plain muted text, not a pill. Give the chips :focus-visible matching .cta-btn, aria-pressed, border:INK_BORDER, and aria-live=polite on a wrapper around the transcript + tl;dr.
acceptance_criteria: Hover lift appears only on things that are clickable; chips keyboard-operable with announced state.
close_reason: fixed in the parallel lane run; build+lint green, verified in-browser at 390/768/820/1280/1440

title: meta: no og/twitter cards, no canonical, no theme-color, favicon.ico 404s
description: index.html has a real title and description but no og: or twitter: tags at all, so sharing the link anywhere produces a bare preview — relevant because the URL is being sent to a reviewer. Also missing: canonical (the apex 307-redirects to www, so the duplicate is real), theme-color, color-scheme, robots.txt, sitemap.xml. /favicon.ico returns 404 and shows in the network tab. apple-touch-icon points at public/snake-blue.png, the abandoned glossy 3D snake rather than the flat vector mascot. Separately, public/snake-blue.svg (the favicon, 21 paths) is a stale duplicate of src/assets/snake-blue.svg (17 paths) and still has artwork defects later commits removed. Detail and exact line references in AUDIT-2026-08-07.md (untracked, repo root).
design: Add og:title/description/image/url/type + twitter:card summary_large_image, canonical to https://www.ssscribe.app/, theme-color #eef4ff, color-scheme light. Generate a 1200x630 og image — a hero screenshot works. Drop a 32x32 favicon.ico into public/, regenerate apple-touch-icon from the current vector, and re-export public/snake-blue.svg from src/assets/.
acceptance_criteria: Link preview renders with image and copy in a validator; no 404s in the network tab on load.
close_reason: fixed in the parallel lane run; build+lint green, verified in-browser at 390/768/820/1280/1440

title: a11y: poke easter egg is a clickable div marked role=presentation, mouse-only
description: snake.tsx:430-431 puts onClick and role='presentation' on adjacent lines of the same div — the code hands the element a handler and in the same breath tells assistive tech it carries no semantics, which ARIA forbids. No tabIndex, no key handler, so the page's one custom interaction is mouse-only. Reused by the CTA snake-letter. Two smaller no-ops in the same handler: the pokeBusy ref at :394 silently drops any re-poke inside the ~0.63s timeline, and the reduced-motion early return at :399-400 does nothing at all while still showing cursor:pointer and the 'poke me' label. eslint has no jsx-a11y plugin so nothing catches it. Detail and exact line references in AUDIT-2026-08-07.md (untracked, repo root).
design: When poke is true render the outer element as <button type='button' aria-label='poke the snake'> with background:none;border:0;padding:0;display:block merged into the existing sizing, and delete the role prop — tiltRef still points at it so GSAP is unaffected. Replace the pokeBusy guard with a stored timeline that restart()s. Add eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y flat.recommended.
acceptance_criteria: Poke reachable by keyboard, announced sensibly, re-pokable; jsx-a11y clean.
close_reason: fixed in the parallel lane run; build+lint green, verified in-browser at 390/768/820/1280/1440

title: DECISION: untrack .beads/ and AGENTS.md from the public repo
description: 12 of 55 tracked files are agent and issue-tracker plumbing: AGENTS.md (line 1 is literally '@CLAUDE.md', the rest is beads boilerplate with a MANDATORY WORKFLOW block) plus 10 files under .beads/ including five git-hook shims and a 0-byte interactions.jsonl. GitHub's file listing is a reviewer's first impression of repo shape. Counter-argument for keeping CLAUDE.md: its theming, styling-approach and snake-mascot sections are the best architectural documentation in the repo. Detail and exact line references in AUDIT-2026-08-07.md (untracked, repo root).
design: git rm -r --cached .beads && git rm --cached AGENTS.md, then add both to .gitignore. Keep CLAUDE.md tracked. Consider lifting its Theming system and Snake mascot sections into README.md. Needs a call on whether untracking .beads/ breaks the Dolt sync workflow.
acceptance_criteria: Decision recorded; if untracked, bd still syncs and the repo file listing reads as a design project.

title: wire the dead links on the messscribe landing
description:
Why now: the Attio Senior Design Engineer application cites ssscribe.app as evidence of a shipped landing page, and a Studio reviewer will click through it. Empty links undercut exactly the craft claim being made.

Scope:
1. Audit every link/CTA on the landing: grep for href="#", href="", empty onClick handlers, buttons with no action. List each with a proposed real target.
2. Mike approves targets BEFORE wiring. Some destinations are product decisions: the app itself is private/single-user at app.ssscribe.app, so get-started-type CTAs cannot link to a signup — options are GitHub, mailto, a demo, or dropping the CTA. Mike's call per link.
3. While in there, flag (do not fix unasked): placeholder title/meta/og tags, missing favicon.
4. Discover how this repo deploys (config files, git remote, ask Mike if ambiguous) and redeploy after the fix.

Out of scope: redesign, copy rewrites, new sections.
acceptance_criteria: No dead or empty links on the live page at ssscribe.app; every target approved by Mike; redeployed and verified live.
close_reason: Shipped in f8f1c0c, live and verified at www.ssscribe.app: 11 links, 0 dead, all three anchor ids resolve. Nav links -> in-page anchors with scroll-padding-top so the sticky nav doesn't cover the landing spot; all three 'add to messenger' CTAs -> https://m.me/61565271402803 (verified to resolve to the bot's Messenger conversation); the 'watch a 20-second demo' ghost button removed, per Mike, because no demo exists; footer rebuilt as real links (3 anchors + github source + mailto) with the 6 entries naming unbuilt things cut. Also fixed while in there: the 'psst - poke me' sticker was sitting on the snake's hit box and swallowing the click it advertises, and the nav CTA wrapped to two lines at 381-411px. Flagged-not-fixed items from the audit are filed as 18 separate issues; detail in AUDIT-2026-08-07.md.

title: dot-grid: lift content above canvas + general polish
description:
dots from the fixed dot-grid canvas (src/components/landing/dot-grid-background.tsx) paint OVER opaque content — visible on the chat preview mockup (white card) in the 'try it in your language' section. root cause: the canvas is position:fixed, and positioned elements paint above non-positioned siblings regardless of DOM order, so any non-positioned opaque surface loses.

suggested fix: wrap PageShell children in a position:relative + z-index:1 container (primitives.tsx) so all content stacks above the canvas; dots stay visible through transparent section backgrounds, but white cards/mockups properly cover them. verify the sticky nav (z-10) and hero art stacking still hold.

while in there, general dot-grid polish ideas: tune BASE_ALPHA/spacing per feedback, consider a subtle accent tint in the cursor halo, and check dpr>2 displays.
close_reason: fixed: PageShell now wraps children in a position:relative/z-index:1 layer so the fixed dot-grid canvas paints behind every section. verified in the built page at 1280px — dots no longer land on the white chat-preview card. the 'general polish' ideas (BASE_ALPHA tuning, accent tint in the cursor halo, dpr>2) were not touched and are not tracked here.

title: transcript tl;dr strings are sentence-case while the storyboard renders the same line lowercase
description:
All six tldr strings in src/lib/transcripts.ts are sentence-case — e.g. 'Flight delayed an hour — arriving ~9:30. Eat without them, save a plate.' and 'Home without keys — left them in the car. Please bring them.' The project rule is lowercase always.

What makes it a defect rather than a style quibble: the storyboard's 'read' card hardcodes the same Portuguese tl;dr as 'flight delayed an hour — arriving ~9:30.' in lowercase. So the identical machine output renders two different ways on one page, roughly a screen apart. Seen side by side in the live preview and the how-it-works section.

The decision underneath it is whether simulated machine output follows the brand voice or imitates what a real bot would emit. Same question as the chat card's 'Active now' and 'Forwarded · voice' chrome. Worth answering once for both, then applying consistently.

Pre-existing — verified unchanged at ec47759, not introduced by the fix run.

title: Section renders an unnamed <section>, so the page's six content sections create no landmarks
description:
The Section primitive (src/components/landing/primitives.tsx) emits a bare <section> with no accessible name. A <section> without one is a generic element, not a landmark, so hero, preview, languages, pricing and CTA are invisible to landmark navigation.

Not a defect blocker: <main> already wraps hero-through-CTA (verified present at ec47759), so axe's region rule passes and no content is orphaned. This is navigation polish, not a failure.

Fix: add an optional label prop to Section that sets aria-label, then pass one at all five call sites — final-cta-section.tsx:9, languages-section.tsx:13, live-preview-section.tsx:15, hero-section.tsx:49, pricing-section.tsx:200. Trivial per site, but it spans five files, which is why it was left out of the parallel lane run.
notes: raised by the lane that fixed the dpe heading semantics; deliberately deferred because it crosses five files that belonged to different lanes

title: body ground ignores the active theme — :root defaults win for any ancestor of the theme class
description:
The theme classes (.theme-messscribe / .theme-whatsscribe) sit on a div inside #root, so <body> has no theme class to inherit from and resolves --bg from the :root defaults instead.

Harmless today: messscribe is the only theme in use and :root now carries exactly its values (set when 0xj was fixed). But if whatsscribe ever ships, the page ground behind the wrapper — the white flash before hydration and the overscroll gutters — stays messscribe blue while the content is green.

Fix: move the theme class onto <html> or <body> rather than the PageShell div, so every ancestor resolves the active theme. Touches index.html and src/components/landing/primitives.tsx.
notes: found by the lane that fixed 0xj (promote tokens to :root); it is the residue of that fix, not a regression from it

title: source indentation split 2-space/4-space with no formatter config
description: The split runs straight through the landing/ folder, so opening site-nav.tsx after hero-section.tsx shows two house styles. src/main.tsx also still carries the Vite scaffold's single-quote no-semicolon style while every other file uses double quotes. No .prettierrc, no .editorconfig, no formatting rules in eslint.config.js. Reads as 'generated in two sittings' rather than one authored system. Note: a PostToolUse formatter hook is already normalizing edited files to 4-space, so touched files are converging on their own. Detail and exact line references in AUDIT-2026-08-07.md (untracked, repo root).
design: Add .prettierrc (4-space matches the majority and all the newer landing components) plus .editorconfig, run prettier over src/, and land it as one isolated 'chore: normalize formatting' commit so it doesn't pollute the design history.
acceptance_criteria: One consistent style across src/; config checked in.

title: unknown URLs hit Vercel's stock 404, and react-router ships for a single static route
description: Verified over the network: https://www.ssscribe.app/nonexistent-path-xyz returns a 404 text/plain page with zero ssscribe identity, so a stale link or a typo in a portfolio submission lands the reviewer on an unbranded error page. There is no vercel.json and no catch-all route. It also means the router does nothing: App.tsx is the first file a source reader opens and it shows BrowserRouter + Routes wrapping one static page, with no <Link> anywhere in the codebase. Detail and exact line references in AUDIT-2026-08-07.md (untracked, repo root).
design: Pick one and commit: either keep the router, add <Route path='*'> and a vercel.json rewrite so the routing contract lives in the repo; or render <MesscribeLanding/> directly and drop react-router-dom.
acceptance_criteria: A typo'd URL lands somewhere branded; App.tsx reads as a deliberate choice either way.
close_reason: fixed in the parallel lane run; build+lint green, verified in-browser at 390/768/820/1280/1440

title: language pills total 48 but the page claims 47 in five places
description: src/lib/transcripts.ts:58-84 has 24 named entries plus '+ 24 more' at :83 = 48. Everything else says 47: the hero sticker (hero-section.tsx:79), the marquee token (marquee.tsx:4), the yellow band eyebrow (languages-section.tsx:22), the receipt line, and index.html's meta description. The pill list sits directly under a heading stating the number, and designers count chips. Detail and exact line references in AUDIT-2026-08-07.md (untracked, repo root).
design: Change :83 to '+ 23 more', or derive it so it cannot drift: `+ ${TOTAL_LANGUAGES - LANGUAGE_PILLS.length} more`.
acceptance_criteria: Chips plus the overflow label sum to the number the copy claims.
close_reason: fixed in the parallel lane run; build+lint green, verified in-browser at 390/768/820/1280/1440

title: dead code in the public repo, and DESIGN.md documents two components that no longer render
description: src/components/phone-frame.tsx is 83 lines marked @deprecated in its own JSDoc with zero references — the only unreferenced component in an otherwise clean src/ (no console.log, no TODO, no commented-out code anywhere, that part is genuinely tidy). It also contains an rgba(255,255,255,0.08) shadow, so anyone grepping the repo for rule violations lands in a file that shouldn't exist. StampedCard in primitives.tsx has zero references too, orphaned when pricing became the receipt. DESIGN.md:243 still lists 'Phone Frame (signature)' as used in the storyboard and :224-233 still specs the two-card pricing layout that commit 45c778f removed. Detail and exact line references in AUDIT-2026-08-07.md (untracked, repo root).
design: git rm src/components/phone-frame.tsx, delete the StampedCard export, and replace the Phone Frame and Cards entries in DESIGN.md with the Receipt (torn clip-path, mono, drop-shadow stamp) as the page's card treatment.
acceptance_criteria: No unreferenced exports in src/; DESIGN.md describes what actually renders.
close_reason: fixed in the parallel lane run; build+lint green, verified in-browser at 390/768/820/1280/1440

title: DESIGN.md violations shipped: rgba blur shadow, frosted nav, shadow token bypass
description: DESIGN.md:194-196 says verbatim that rgba(0,0,0,0.1) or any non-zero blur radius is 'the ai default, not this brand'. chat-preview.tsx:115 ships boxShadow '0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,0.06)' — grep -rn rgba src/ is the first thing a design-engineering reviewer runs on a public repo. DESIGN.md:274 also says 'Don't use blur, frosted glass, glassmorphism', but site-nav.tsx:21-22 is backdropFilter blur(12px) over a 90%-alpha background — the only soft surface on a page built from flat color, and it's on screen during most of the scroll. DESIGN.md:238 contradicts :274 by describing 'backdrop blur on scroll' for the nav, so the doc needs reconciling too. Separately six distinct shadow values ship on a page whose SHADOWS token object declares exactly two, and the token is bypassed where it exists (hero-section.tsx:75-77,:164,:183). Detail and exact line references in AUDIT-2026-08-07.md (untracked, repo root).
acceptance_criteria: grep for rgba and blur in src/ returns only intentional alpha borders; shadows come from the token object; DESIGN.md self-consistent.
close_reason: fixed in the parallel lane run; build+lint green, verified in-browser at 390/768/820/1280/1440

title: semantics: storyboard steps, pricing commentary and footer labels are divs, not headings
description: Pressing H in a screen reader yields six headings for a page that visually presents roughly fifteen. The three storyboard step names (storyboard.tsx:62-70,173-181,265-273 at 22px/800), both halves of the pricing argument (pricing-section.tsx:143-155 and :168-180 at up to 32px/800) and the footer column labels (site-footer.tsx) are all divs. The h1/h2 levels that do exist are correct and unskipped, which makes the omission read as oversight rather than a system. Related: the final CTA h2's accessible text is 'okay, ssold?' — the snake stands in for the first s and is correctly aria-hidden, but nothing replaces the letter, so the punchline reads as a typo in any heading-outline tool or crawler. Detail and exact line references in AUDIT-2026-08-07.md (untracked, repo root).
design:
Render those as

with margin:0 — zero visual change. Add s before the snake slot in final-cta-section.tsx. While in that file, pointerEvents:none on the oversizing wrapper span at :44 (its 1.32em box inside a 0.72em slot overhangs the comma and the following s, so hovering plain heading text shows a hand cursor) and re-enable it on the inner Snake.
acceptance_criteria: Heading outline matches what the page visually presents; CTA heading reads 'okay, sssold?'.
close_reason: fixed in the parallel lane run; build+lint green, verified in-browser at 390/768/820/1280/1440

title: snake blue is not the brand blue, and the CTA headline puts them side by side
description: src/assets/snake-blue.svg body gradient runs #0073F4 to #028CFE (mid ~#0180F9) against --accent #3b82f6. In the hero they're far enough apart to forgive, but the CTA headline puts the snake in the 's' slot of 'sssold?', so a saturated blue letterform butts against two lighter accent-blue letters in the same word. The nav lockup has the same adjacency. It's the page's punchline and the one place the mismatch is unmissable. Detail and exact line references in AUDIT-2026-08-07.md (untracked, repo root).
design: Retune the body gradient stops to sit on --accent as the mid value. Since the SVG is injected inline for GSAP, fill='var(--accent)' on the body path also works and makes the green theme swap for free.
acceptance_criteria: Snake and accent blue read as one color family in the CTA headline.
